# SHA-256 reduced to 39 steps: ordinary collision by the transplanted pair with two released state words (k = 4) on the fibre h4 = 0x3cc9eebe; the list generated by rule at import, the W17 condition solved on 18-bit prefixes by a generic counted pass

History: our ae2d3c1c (time 94.1805, memory 2^20.0000) was accepted with steps (1)-(4) below; a26bcf74 is ae2d3c1c with step (5) only; this entry is a26bcf74 with step (6) only (the k4d cap 944). (1) The tail is priced at 2^-74.3238 under a new declared MODEL premise of this entry, H2-transfer, with screened-window scope (Sections 8 and 10): the designated mate's tail on the fibre 0x3cc9eebe is taken at the linear mean of the 14 organizer-executed runs r39-tail-01..14 of the unchanged replica, which sample the advice draws (the value of 5f8e6192's H2, measured there on the advice, not on this fibre). 0b62ed88 refiled f429192b: the second-order term no longer rests on any window-moment reduction; it is bounded for any correlation by a cap of 1,024 evaluated claws per window and the measured maximum within-claw co-hit rate over every listed key (Section 7). It also refiles 209b4410: its time is priced by a second-order Bonferroni bound over ALL W17 key hits of a window, on designated-mate events: no hit is selected or ordered, every hit enters symmetrically, and the bound holds for any dependence between the tails of different hits (Section 7). The number sits next to 209b4410's but comes from a different derivation in which no hit is ordered or selected. Trials are distinct keys, with no premise on how the tails of a key's mates depend on each other (it also refiles 9a255e58). It is our w13 program (the line of 837b7139 and 089cd791) with one lever: the k = 4 list is re-based from the advice fibre h0 = 0x36faf0de to the fibre h4 = 0x3cc9eebe, and it is generated at import by a rule instead of being decoded from a shipped recipe. On the new fibre the list has 9,701,592 entries in 728 classes (3,462,264 distinct (a2, kappa) keys, 200 kappa groups, 62,400 distinct 18-bit prefixes), against 821,520 entries in 256 classes on h0. The walk constant c9 and the F9 constant C9 shift by h4 - h0 = 0x05cefde0; nothing else of the construction moves (Section 2.3). A trial is a distinct (a2, kappa) key with at least one listed entry passing F8 in a claw passing F9 (Section 7). Counting every hit follows a7b383d1 (credited). The list is Jbenisek's construction of f92b8068 continued to a new fibre; the walk, claw filters and tail replica are the line of 3aa063d1 (Jbenisek, dariolina, sraiw, newjordan). The work cap is measured on 60 screened full windows of the shipped attack path (Section 7, Appendix B); the trial count is measured on 2,000 F9 claws of 0b62ed88's 48 unscreened full windows (Section 7, Appendix A) and carried to the screened law by the declared premise H1-screen (Section 10).

Labels: MEASURED = run by us with the shipped program's counters or with the named tool; DERIVED = arithmetic from stated numbers; CITED = measured and published by the named earlier entry.

## 1. Target and output
- **Target.** `sha256-r39-prefix-v1`: SHA-256 with the first 39 steps in every compression, standard IV, FIPS 180-4 padding, feed-forward, all 256 output bits.
- **Output.** Two distinct 128-byte messages M0 || M1 and M0 || M1': the same random first block M0, second blocks with M1' = M1 + DL (word-wise modular, differences in words 8..12). Equal lengths, identical padding block. Ordinary collision.
- **Claim.** time_log2 = 94.1584, memory_log2_bytes = 20.0000, preprocessing_log2 = 43, advice 160 bytes = 2^7.32193, success probability 0.39. The time is total charged work (work cap, one-time setup, 2^43 preprocessing), ceiled at the fourth decimal; the memory is the peak over the phases of the run, 1,013,513 bytes, plus 32,768 bytes of headroom, claimed at 2^20.

## 2. The construction
**2.1 Advice.** The 39-step semi-free-start pair of 5f8e6192 (CV_PUB, MP_PUB, M_PUB; 160 bytes), on the characteristic of ePrint 2026/1120 Tables 21 and 23 (CITED from 293ca62c and 38912d66). No recipe is shipped: the advice is the 160-byte pair only.

**2.2 The transplant, k = 4.** As in w13: fix A[8..11], E[12..15] and W12..W15 to the advice values; for any cv and (a0, a1, a2, a3) = A[4..7] the words W0..W11 follow (`k4_words`). W9 = C - a1 + h4(a2, a3) with h4 = MAJ(A8, a3, a2) - CH(E12, E11, E10), E10 = a2 + t(a3), E11 = a3 + c11; W10 = kappa(a3) - a2; W11 depends on a3 only; W0 and W1 do not depend on (a2, a3).

**2.3 The fibre is a parameter.** On any fibre h4(a2, a3) = h, W9 = C - a1 + h is one value per claw, F9 stays a per-claw test, and W16 = s1(W14) + W9 + s0(W1) + W0 is one value per claw. Taking h = FIB = 0x3cc9eebe instead of the advice's h0 = 0x36faf0de shifts the walk constant c9 and the F9 constant C9 by K4_HD = FIB - h0 = 0x05cefde0 (computed by the program from the advice). A claw of the shifted walk map then gives W16 = g for every entry of the new list. The advice (a2, a3) itself is not on the new fibre, so the base variant is not a trial and its path is removed from `claw()`; the transplant-claw experiment no longer claws the advice (an h0 claw). MEASURED on the built program (build/e2e15.py, from w15/tools/check15s.py): all F9 claws of windows 1000 and 1014 of the shipped program x 20 listed entries each, 35,940 (claw, entry) cases: W1 = u, W16 = g, W9 = C9 + HD - a1 in F9, both messages on the advice trail through step 16, the advice states after step 17 at a W17 hit; failures none.

**2.4 What remains after a claw.** Per claw: W9 in F9. Per entry: W8 in F8 (density 9/128), and W17 = advice value; then the tail (Section 8). Two entries with the same a2 and kappa (mates) pass or fail W17 together; they differ in a3, hence in W11, W3..W8 and every tail word.

**2.5 The list by rule (MEASURED and DERIVED).**
- Classes: a3 = (E11adv XOR m) - c11 for every submask m of CUBE = 0xf74400da (14 bits, 16,384 masks), kept when W11C - a3 lies in F11: 1,536 candidates. CUBE is the OR of the E11 masks of the 728 classes of the exhaustive enumeration; the rule R2 of our list-ceiling note (E11 AND 0x08b81020 fixed) holds on the whole cube because the two masks are disjoint.
- Entries of a class: every a2 with (R3) h4(a2, a3) = FIB, (R4) W10 = kappa(a3) - a2 in F10, (R5) bit 30 of E10 equal to bit 30 of E11.
- **The rule set equals the exhaustive list.** enum15 scans all 2^32 values of a3 and checks every candidate entry on the real two-message trail at the advice point and three random points (0 mixed verdicts, 0 failures of every identity it checks; 9,701,592 valid entries in 728 classes). build/rule15.c generates the rule set and compares it with that list as sorted (a3, a2) sets: equal; at h0 the same rule gives exactly the 821,520-entry list of f92b8068.
- F10 is a set of bit conditions on W10 (D10 = 0xc0000000, T10 = 0x087ff000): w2^w13 = 1, w9^w26 = 1, w15 = w19, and either w30 = 1, or w30 = 0 with w3^w14 = w10^w27 = w31 = 1^w16^w20. Checked over all 2^32 values: 301,989,888 members, 0 mismatches.
- **Generator.** A bit-serial automaton over a2 (the fibre's carry and borrow, the borrow of kappa - a2, the captured W10 bits, the F10 branch) is solved backwards, bit-sliced over 256 candidate classes per 256-bit word (`_k4fe`); then a depth-first search with exact pruning lists the 18-bit prefixes of each class (`_k4lf`). Classes are taken in kappa order, and a group's prefix set becomes 18 bit planes per block of 256 lanes when the next group begins (`_k4fin`). One sample entry per group is kept for the planted checks.
- **Table.** 200 kappa groups, 728 classes (at most 8 per group), 62,400 prefixes in 300 blocks (at most 1,024 prefixes per group). MEASURED: group by group, the prefix sets built at import equal those of the exhaustive list, and every sample entry satisfies the rule. Counts asserted at import.

## 3. The W17 pass
**3.1 The equation.** As in w13: s0(y) = y + r with y = a2 + w and r = kd + W17 - u - w; the low 18 bits of y determine the other 14, and 18 bit checks remain.

**3.2 The pass (`k4q`).** The routine of w13, unchanged except two lines (Section 3.4). Per evaluated F9 claw: spill and restore (624), a1 and w (55), the 18 constant words (54); per group 110; per block 403. **K4_PASS = 733 + sum over the 200 groups of (110 + 403 x blocks) = 143,633, the same for every claw**, asserted at import. A survivor costs 711 plus 563 per class of its group tested: at most 711 + 563 x 8 = 5,215. A key hit tests the classes of its group as mates: at most 8 x (560 + 2 x 2,812) = 49,472.

**3.3 Same hits.** A listed key satisfies W17 in a claw if and only if its prefix lane survives and the scalar test accepts it. MEASURED by the gate on 6 real F9 claws of the shipped program's windows: for each of the 200 groups a planted key (the group's sample entry, its W17 placed as the target) is found by the pass, and the counted cost is the group's pass cost plus 711 + 563 x (classes tested) per survivor. The organizer experiment repeats it for all 200 groups on the first F9 claw of each window (Section 11).

**3.4 Changes against w13.** (i) The fibre: c9, C9 shifted; k4q's W9 reference is the claw's own W9, C9 + HD - a1, not the advice's; the mates of a key hit are the classes of its group, not the 4,096 submasks of 0xf1c000da. (ii) The list by rule: no recipe literal, no inflate reader, no decoder; the per-key diagnostic runs over the entries of every 50th group (four groups) and only in the experiment modes. (iii) The walk table: 97 x 1,024 = 99,328 slots of 40 bits, 15,520 words, the largest table under 2^20 with the other rows of Section 6. The slot of a 25-bit distinguished value r is (97 r) >> 15 = ((r << 6) + (r << 5) + r) >> 15 through the counter; 2^15 / 97 = 338 < 512, so slot and the 9 check bits determine r. Keep-longer rule as in w13.

**3.5 Routine by routine against w13** (every routine of the source compared; module lines with constants are listed in Section 5). Changed: `consts` (c9 + K4_HD); `Attack.base_setup` (only C9, shifted, is left); `Attack.claw` (the base-variant path removed; check mode asserts the claw's W9 against a listed entry); `Attack.hit` (slot (97 r) >> 15 and its check); `P` (WDIG of 15,520 words); `k4q` (the claw's W9; mates among the group's classes); `k4f` (the diagnostic over the four groups of `_k4ind`); `_k4fin` (planes of one group from its prefix set); `k4_budget` (G and the second-order divisor 1 - 0.07579); `_e1` (transplant-claw: advice checks and the fibre checks per group; random transplants with a listed entry); `_k4e` (no base F8 count; the acceptance constants). Removed: `_w3gen`, `_k4c1`, `_sm`. Added: `_k4st`, `_k4fe`, `_k4lf`, `_k4cls`, `_k4build`, `_k4ind`, `h4ok`. Every other routine is byte-identical to w13's. This entry against 0b62ed88: `P` (SCREEN = 1, KCAP = 679, KCAP0 = 710 for the screen-off path, DTRY = 8,192), `k4_scr` (added), `Attack.__init__` (the screen flag), `Attack.window_setup` (the screen in the draw loop, Section 3.6), `K4_OPS_PER_CLAW`, `k4_budget` and the import assertion (Section 5), `_k4e` (the four asserted windows run with the screen off; trial 0 adds one screened window, Section 11).

**3.6 Pre-generation screen (credited to 0xplemonade's a3eb4a8a; its masks, threshold, KCAP = 679 and DTRY = 8,192 unchanged).** Each drawn first block's chaining value is scored before kernel generation: from `consts5` of the CV (cw, eb, P, R; 4 ops to pack), S = 3 pop(R & 0x00F27618) + 2 pop(R & 0x7F0D89E6) + 2 eb[1] + eb[2] + P[31] - pop(P & 0x1FFFFFFE), charged 183 ops per draw, a3eb4a8a's counted figure, kept here as a conservative charge above an explicit v5 form of at most 65 ops: with A = pop(R & 0x00F27618), B = pop(R & 0x7F0D89E6), C = pop(P & 0x1FFFFFFE), each count is the SWAR sequence x -= (x >> 1) & 0x55555555 (3); x = (x & 0x33333333) + ((x >> 2) & 0x33333333) (4); x = (x + (x >> 4)) & 0x0f0f0f0f (3); x += x >> 8 (2); x += x >> 16 (2); x &= 63 (1), 15 ops, so 3 counts plus 3 input masks = 48; eb[1], eb[2], P[31] extracted in 5; 3A, 2B, 2eb[1] in 4; the nonnegative S + 28 = 3A + 2B + 2eb[1] + eb[2] + P[31] + (28 - C) formed and compared, branch included, in at most 8. The program's host bit count, bin().count('1'), evaluates the same predicate; it is not a charged unit op, and the 183 charged ops per draw exceed the 65. A block with S > 5 is discarded (3 more ops) and the next block is drawn (its draw and first-block compression charged as before); a kept block goes to the unchanged exact kernel gate, which now accepts at most 679 records (KCAP; 710 in the base). A window stops after 8,192 discarded draws or 32 rejected generations, every charge counted. The screen consumes no randomness. Its effect on work enters the price only through the re-measured window totals (H6, Appendix B) and C_W; its effect on the window law and the trial count is the new premise H1-screen (Section 10).

- **Claimed: memory_log2_bytes = 20.0000.** The peak over the three phases is the walk phase, 1,013,513 bytes; with 32,768 bytes of headroom that is 1,046,281 bytes, within 2^20. The program asserts 32 x (table + queue + planes) + 315,369 + 32,768 <= 2^20. A table of 98 x 1,024 slots would not fit.
- **Phases** as in w13. S is the import: module data, code and the generator's working memory; when the import returns no generator, feasibility table or builder frame is alive and no attack object exists (MEASURED, audit with the cycle collector off). G and W as in w13, re-audited on this program. Phase W exceeds G by 503,630 and S by 357,448 bytes. The row total is not a memory state.
- **Rows.** Walk rows and the 4,111-instruction walk census as in w13 (CITED from 9993eaa8 there; this program's executed-block census does not exceed w13's). The prefix table: 300 x 18 x 32 = 172,800 bytes of planes plus lane counts, group constants, 728 class words and 200 sample keys. The setup rows are measured on the generator (build/genmem15.py): largest feasibility table of a 256-lane chunk 1,947 lane words and 14,673 key scalars, transition memo at most 213 keys and 285 children, search stack 16, largest group 1,024 prefixes. No recipe, decoder or inflate row remains. The walk-kernel generator rows are the maxima over 300 random chaining values (776 graph records, 11,451 characters); run on the chaining values of all 48 shipped windows the generator stays below them (710 records, 10,567 characters). Phase G lies 503,630 bytes under phase W, so the generator rows would have to grow about tenfold to move the peak.
- **Code.** Every k4 instruction has a row, at 36 bytes: one instruction per syntactic operation of every k4 routine, the generator and the experiment diagnostics included (1,346), plus the pass in looped machine form (1,246): 2,592 instructions.
- **What the table covers.** All memory the `--attack` path allocates, setup included, and all k4 code. The screen (Section 3.6) keeps only the scalars of one draw (four packed words and S, 20 bytes, transient), inside the 32,768-byte headroom; the kernel-image rows stay at 710 records, above the screened path's KCAP = 679. The experiment modes allocate on top of it the diagnostic's entry blocks and statistics; the `--attack` path never allocates them.

## 7. Success probability and the cap
- **Trials.** A trial is a distinct (a2, kappa) key with at least one listed entry passing F8, in a claw passing F9. Mates of a key share W17 and differ in a3, hence in W11, W3..W8 and every tail word from W18 on (Section 2.4). When a key hits W17 the program tests every class of its group, so every mate passing F8 is compressed; the key succeeds if any of them does, so with probability at least that of any one of them. No independence and no other relation between the tails of mates is used.
- **Count: 9041.6 per distinct claw (cap 944; a26bcf74 uncapped: 9044.1).** On 2,000 real F9 claws of 0b62ed88's unscreened program (16 batches of 125: the first 125 F9 claws, in arrival order, of windows 1000 to 1015) the distinct keys with an entry in F8 number 576,745.3 per F9 claw (s.e. 970.3 from the batch means; per-claw s.d. 57,687). The distinct F9 claws per window are measured on the 60 screened 2^26 windows of the shipped program (Appendix B, F9 distinct column, counted on the full key set of each window): 54,430 in total, mean 907.1667, sample s.d. 25.6780, range 855 to 959. Joint one-sided 99% lower bound (union bound, 99.5% on each factor; independent windows and batches, Student-t): T >= (576,745.3 - t(15, 0.995) x 970.3) x (907.1667 - t(59, 0.995) x 25.6780 / sqrt(60)) / 57,003.18 = 573,886.10 x 898.3429 / 57,003.18 = 9044.17, with t(15, 0.995) = 2.946713 and t(59, 0.995) = 2.661759; priced as 9044.1 (rounded down) -- a26bcf74's figure. THIS ENTRY (cap 944): the F9-claw factor is taken on the ADMITTED claws of the same 60 windows, D_i' = min(D_i, 944) (Appendix B, F9 distinct column; 3 windows exceed 944: seeds 802001, 802013, 802043, 38 claws): mean 906.5333, s.d. 24.5602, one-sided 99.5% bound 906.5333 - 2.661759 x 24.5602 / sqrt(60) = 898.0937; T >= 573,886.10 x 898.0937 / 57,003.18 = 9041.66, priced 9041.6. C_W = 57,003.18 is the declared H1-screen model mean, as in B and the cap. (ae2d3c1c priced 8956.4: 898.625 unscreened F9 claws per window over 48 windows, divided by 57,010.58, estimate 9090.904 with s.e. 51.689, minus t(15) = 2.602 x s.e.) Counted by w15/tools/f8count.exe over the exhaustive list, which equals the rule set (Section 2.5). Taking the first claws of a window is not a selection on the count: on all F9 claws of windows 1000 and 1001 the first 125 average 580,014 and 576,395 keys against 577,913 and 574,102 for the rest (Welch z = +0.39, +0.40). Observation, not a premise and not priced: the same claws have 682,518.4 F8-passing entries per F9 claw, 1.1834 per key. Window 1000 is also the window on which the fibre was compared with its neighbours (in an earlier build of the walk, 908 claws there); its 125 claws are 1/16 of this sample and their mean, 580,014 keys, lies within the spread of the other windows (one-way ANOVA over the 16 windows: F = 0.564 on 15 and 1,984 df, between-window s.d. estimated 0). These claws are of 0b62ed88's unscreened program; for the screened program of this entry the key count per F9 claw is carried by the declared premise H1-screen (Section 10), and at least 9041.6 trial keys per distinct claw is priced. The F9-claw factor is of the screened windows themselves: 907.17 per window (s.d. 25.68) in the 60 screened windows of Appendix B, against 898.62 in the 48 unscreened windows.

- **Success: second-order Bonferroni over all key hits (counting every hit, as a7b383d1 does; credited for that only).** (i) The program tests every W17 key hit of every window: `k4q` (experiments/r39joint_k4.py lines 1042-1057) runs over every survivor lane of every group, and at each key hit compresses every class of the group whose words pass W9, W17 and F8 (lines 1050-1056, 560 per class and 2 x 2,812 per compressed pair, inside the window's counted work and priced in K as key-hit work); after a hit without collision the loops continue, and a window stops early only on a collision (line 804). At most m_max = 944 distinct F9 claws are evaluated per window (`k4d`, line 1106: a distinct F9 claw is inserted only while the window's claw table holds fewer than 944; a26bcf74: 1,024 -- this entry's one change). (ii) For a trial key k let its designated mate be its lowest-a3 class whose entry passes F8 in the claw, and B_k the event that the designated mate's pair collides; B_k is contained in the key's success, because the program compresses every mate, and p'_k = P(B_k | claws). (iii) Given the hits, the window succeeds with probability at least P(union over hit k of B_k) >= sum over hits of p'_k - sum over hit pairs k < l of P(B_k and B_l) (second-order Bonferroni, for any number H of hits). Each pair term is at most min(p'_k, p'_l) <= (p'_k + p'_l) / 2, whatever the joint law of the tails, so the pair sum is at most sum over hit k of p'_k x (number of other hit keys) / 2. The designated-mate events are used, not the key's whole success event: the coefficient is negative for H >= 4, so the measured lower bound may be substituted only where the probability itself is the designated mate's, which arm K measures. (iv) Average over the hits given the claws (H5): each trial key is hit with probability q = 2^-32; keys of different claws are hit independently; inside one claw W17 = G(a2, kappa, w) + c(claw) with w and c fixed by the claw, so two keys of a claw are hit together exactly when their G values coincide, which the program-independent count sweep/cohit.c measures at 1.336 times the independent pair rate (512 random w, all 3,462,264 keys). Hence E[pair sum | claws] <= sum over k of p'_k [q^2 (n_w - D_c(k)) + q pi_k] / 2, with D_c(k) the trial keys of k's claw and pi_k its expected co-hit partners in that claw. The cross-claw part is q^2 sum over claws c of P_c (m_w - 1) mu_D after averaging the other claws' key counts, which are functions of their own (a0, a1) only and i.i.d. across the claws of a window (H1-screen): since m_w <= m_max by the program, it is at most q^2 (m_max - 1) mu_D P_w for ANY dependence between the number of claws and the tails, with mu_D <= 579,271 (the 99% bound, rounded up of the keys per claw, 576,745 + 2.602 x 970). Within a claw, both keys of a pair hit iff their G values coincide. The Bonferroni sum is taken over the sub-collection of hits whose equal-G cluster in the claw has at most 4 keys; a union over fewer events is still a lower bound, and the choice depends on the claw's (w, c) only, not on any tail. For a kept key N_k(w) <= 3, so its pair term is (q/2) p'_k min(N_k(w), 3). Averaged over w (independent of the tails, H5) it is at most (q/2) p'_k pi_max with pi_max = 1.36e-2, the family-wise bound (alpha = 0.001, all keys, two runs of 16,384 random w: 1.3556e-02 and 1.3355e-02) on E[min(N_k, 3)] for every listed key. The left-out hits lose at most q p'_k P(N_k >= 4) of the first-order term, with P(N_k >= 4) <= ln(3,462,264 / 0.001) / 16,384 = 0.001341 for every key (no N >= 4 for any key in 16,384 w; family-wise at alpha = 0.001). Participant tools: w15/sweep/cohit2.c (output w15/sweep/cohit2_16384.txt), w15/sweep/cohit3.c (w15/sweep/cohit3_16384.txt), w15/sweep/nf.c (w15/sweep/nf.txt: s0(y) - y has at most 14 preimages, so N_k(w) <= 2,799; not needed by the bound). Both terms are bounded for every key, so they hold whatever the correlation between partner rates and tails across keys. c2 = 2^-32 x 943 x 579,271 / 2 + 1.36e-2 / 2 = 0.063592 + 0.006800 = 0.070392, and the divisor is 1 - c2 - 0.001341 = 1 - 0.071733, priced as the conservative literal 1 - 0.071734 (a26bcf74 with m_max 1,024: 1 - 0.077129). No moment of the window size, no correlation and no allowance enters. Over windows, E[q P_w] = E[n_w] q p_key with p_key the designated-mate tail weighted by trial keys (H2-transfer; arm K weighted by window size). (v) Windows are independent (fresh first blocks): P(no success) <= product over windows of (1 - P(window success)) <= exp(-lambda). No hit is selected or ordered; every hit enters symmetrically; the bound holds for any dependence between the tails of different hits. Hence lambda = B x G x 9041.6 x 2^-32 x 2^-74.3238 x (1 - 0.071734) = -ln 0.61 + 2^-40, set in `k4_budget`; success 0.39. The pair term costs 0.1074 bit. (vi) Real W17 hits at probability 2^-32 were observed: the 48 windows had 37 key hits against 38.58 expected over all 200 groups (dispersion chi-square 34.35 on 47 df); of them, 3 F8-passing mates were compressed against 6.85 expected (Poisson P = 0.09, adverse and not significant; disclosed).
- **The cap does not bind (H6, screened whole-window bound).** The cap is set from the measured totals of whole screened windows, not from per-component bounds: a window's total is the shipped counter `m.o` over `Attack.run_window()` (every screen draw and discard, the base walk, the k4d gate and insertion, every pass at its own count, every survivor and key-hit charge), so the covariance of the components and the online screen charges (4 + 183 per draw, 3 per discarded draw) are inside it. Sample: 60 pre-declared windows (seeds 802000-802059, 2^26 walk evaluations, attack path with the screen on, k4 on, all 60 present; Appendix B): mean 590,167,957.5, s.d. 6,075,985.2. H6 model: the screened window totals are i.i.d. over windows and the normal-theory Student-t and chi-square bounds hold for their mean and s.d. One-sided 99.75% bound on the mean, t(59, 0.9975) = 2.9164: 592,455,631.3, used as 592,455,632; one-sided 99.75% bound on the s.d., chi-square(59, 0.0025) = 33.048: 8,118,408.3; jointly 99.5%. These are bounds on the mean and s.d. of the window distribution, not a maximum over windows. Cap per window 10,394 x 57,003.18 = 592,491,052.92: margin 35,420.92 operations per window. For independent windows, Chebyshev on the sum over this entry's B = 104,911,625,030,078,251,925,505 windows (applied to the accepted program's same-seed reference work by J-168's pathwise domination, see the claw-cap paragraph) bounds the probability that the cap binds before B windows by s^2 / (B x margin^2) = 5.01e-19 with the bounded s.d. and 2.80e-19 with the sample s.d. (a26bcf74 at its B 105,495,757,033,739,569,332,225: 4.98e-19, below the 2^-40 slack inside lambda. The harness (winmeasure_rival.py) restores the counter around its non-charging yield hooks, so they add no priced work. The import assertion also checks K >= 590,167,958 / 57,003.18 = 10,353.25: a panel-mean sanity check of the observed mean cost per claw, not a separate upper bound; H6 supplies the cap justification.
- **The claw cap (m_max = 944) binds in 3 of the 60 panel windows, by design.** In the accepted panel (Appendix B) the distinct F9 claws per window reach 959 (969 in 0b62ed88's 48 unscreened windows); with this entry's cap the claws beyond the 944th in arrival order (seeds 802001, 802013, 802043: 38 claws in total) are charged the 12-operation k4d lookup and are not inserted or evaluated. The trial bound therefore uses the ADMITTED claws, D_i' = min(D_i, 944) (Section 7, Count). In the organizer windows at most 11 F9 claws occur, so every k4d call there takes the same branch as without the cap; the cap branch is the single comparison `len(T) < 944` at line 1106. H6 (J-168): the whole-window work of the capped program is dominated pathwise by the accepted program's on the same seed (same 12-operation k4d check per claw; no more k4q calls than the uncapped run-to-completion window), so the SUM of capped window work is at most the sum of the same-seed uncapped reference work and the accepted H6 Chebyshev bound (mean 590,167,957.5, s.d. 6,075,985.2, bounded s.d. 8,118,408.3) applies to that reference sum at this entry's B: cap-exhaustion risk 5.01e-19 (2.80e-19 with the sample s.d.). The capped program's own work distribution is NOT re-measured and no variance bound for it is claimed. **The last window.** The cap is checked between windows; one window's k4 work is at most 944 x (143,633 + 62,400 x (5,215 + 49,472)) = 3.22e12 operations by the cap (every lane a survivor with 8 classes and a key hit), and the whole screened window total was at most 605,480,625 operations in the 60 windows; even 1,000 times that plus the k4 bound keeps one window under 2^42 operations, 2^42 / 2,812 compressions, which is added to the total charged work (Section 5) and to the program's time assertion.

- `experiments/r39tail.py` is w13's file, byte-identical: the replica with QDECL = -74.54, run by the organizer as r39-tail-01..14. It is a new, favorable declared heuristic of this entry, not inherited from 5f8e6192's acceptance, offered under the exploratory lane's standard for declared heuristics with relevant evidence (JUDGE_LANES.md, lines 55-65). The replica's check value QDECL = -74.54 is unchanged; pricing at it instead would add 0.2162 bit. **Screened scope.** The premise explicitly covers trial keys drawn from windows of this entry's screened chaining-value law (Section 3.6); the arms below drew their claws from unscreened windows, so the earlier new-fibre measurements and 0b62ed88's acceptance are evidence for the unscreened law, and the transfer to screened windows is part of the declared premise (the carrier sees a window only through its claws' (a0, a1), which H1-screen declares independent of the chaining value). 0b62ed88's further runs, recomputed from the run files of w13 (build/tail15.py):

- **Transfer to the variants of the new fibre (MEASURED by this entry's previous seat, participant-run, not organizer-executed; w15/tail, re-analysed here).** The organizer's replica r39-tail-01..14 samples W8 in F8 and W9 in F9 on the advice values of W10, W11, not the new fibre's class-01 entries. Joint arms replace W8..W11 per lane by real words: R arms take (claw, entry) uniformly over F8-passing pairs on real F9 claws (w13 windows for h0, windows of the shifted walk for 3cc9eebe; every claw asserted in F9 under its fibre); S arms take W9, W8 from their filters and (W10, W11) from a uniform entry. The R arm weights entries uniformly; the attack's trials are keys. The key-weighted arm K below measures the attack's quantity directly. Every arm on the organizer seed protocol (ids r39-tail-15..42 for R, 15..28 for S), with the identical SMC carrier for equal ids, so paired differences cancel the carrier; every hit verified by recompressing both blocks.

- Paired, R 3cc9eebe - R h0 over 28 runs: log2 ratio of linear means -0.014 (s.e. 0.023); pooled hits -0.0105 (Poisson s.e. 0.0181). One-sided 99% bound on the loss: -0.014 - 2.473 x 0.023 = -0.071 bit, so a loss above 0.071 bit is excluded at 99%. Sensitivity: in the attack every trial has a0 even and W1 odd (class 01); the pool arms back-solve W1 with either parity, and the class-01-only paired figure is -0.021. Real variants of either fibre do not do worse than the shipped draws (R 3cc9eebe - adv: +0.023, s.e. 0.032). Row survival 25/24, 26/25, 27/26, 28/27 equal within noise. - **Key-weighted arm K (participant-run, w15/tail/mkpoolk.c, armk.sh, analyzek.py).** Per proposal: a claw drawn uniformly from the F9 claws of window 1000 + i - 15 of the shipped program (run i), and a distinct (a2, kappa) key drawn uniformly from the list, kept if the key has a mate passing F8 in that claw; the proposed words are those of its designated mate, the lowest-a3 class passing F8 (ascending a3 is the order in which k4q tests them). So (claw, key) is uniform over the pairs in which the key is a trial, as the hit keys of the attack are (every trial key is hit with the same probability 2^-32), and the proposal is the designated mate's pair, which the program compresses at every hit of that key; no reweighting and no premise on mates. Same ids r39-tail-15..42, same SMC carrier as R, every hit verified and its (a0..a3) recovered. Result: mean 2^-74.3734, one-sided 99% bound 2^-74.4662, **one-sided 99.9% bound 2^-74.5035** (Student t, 27 df, 3.421); class-01 only (2 x c01) 2^-74.3528, its 99.9% bound 2^-74.4887. Weighted by the number of evaluated claws of each run's window (the attack weights windows by their trials): mean 2^-74.3747, one-sided 99.9% bound 2^-74.5058; correlation of window size and run tail -0.19. Model, stated plainly: the SMC carrier sees a window only through its claws' (a0, a1). Paired against the entry-weighted R arm (same carrier): +0.0047 bit (s.e. 0.0172). Accepted keys had 1.1857 F8-passing mates on average in the first run.

**Transfer to the new fibre.** Priced directly on the new fibre, the R 3cc9eebe arm alone (28 runs, mean -74.3781) has the one-sided 99.9% bound 2^-74.4804 (Student t, 27 df, 3.421), above the replica's check value 2^-74.54. The R-arm claws came from windows of the shifted walk of an earlier build (previous seat's tools; seed 1000 gave 908 F9 claws there against 871 in the shipped program's window 1000), so the arm uses real F9 claws of the same walk map but not the shipped program's own windows. The figure that matches the attack exactly would be the class-01-only paired one, and it is inside the same bound.

## 9. Advice construction and preprocessing (H3)
As in w13 Section 9: the pair of 5f8e6192, chosen among 93 candidate pairs; 93 x 2^36 = 2^42.5392 constructions plus 93 x 14 x 2^24 = 2^34.35 screens, 2^42.545 in all, declared as preprocessing_log2 = 43 and added to the claimed time. The organizer experiment runs the fibre search on the shipped pair (g16_fibre_size = 2, g17_fibre_size = 1, fibre_dfs_ops = 1,944) and the 256-candidate slice (advice_slice_hits = 1, ops_per_cand = 411). The list is built at import inside K4_SETUP; the choice of the fibre is a one-time offline search: about 7,000 fibres scored (at most 2^36 operations), five enumerated exhaustively by enum15 (per fibre 2^32 F11 tests of about 20 operations, 2^36.3, plus the real two-message trail at four points on at most 1.8 x 10^8 F10-passing solutions at about 10^3 operations each, 2^39.4; five fibres 2^41.8), their F8 counts on about 950 real claws each (9.7 x 10^6 entries x 50 operations per claw, 2^38.7 each, 2^41.0 for five) and one window per fibre: at most 2^42.6 operations, 2^31.1 compressions in all (EST from the tools' loop counts), against the 2^41.1 compressions left between the 2^42.545 of the advice and the declared 2^43.

## 10. Premises, and the limits of their evidence
- **H1-screen (new, MODEL, declared heuristic; score-setting).** Under the screened chaining-value and window law of the shipped program (S <= 5, KCAP = 679, DTRY = 8,192, KTRY = 32; production window 2^26 walk evaluations): (i) the distinct claws per window have mean 57,003.18 (the 60-window panel mean of Appendix B, s.d. 210.99), the unit C_W of B and of the cap; (ii) the trials, distinct (a2, kappa) keys with an entry in F8 in a claw passing F9, number at least 9,041.6 per distinct claw; (iii) kept chaining values are independent across windows; the (a0, a1) of the distinct F9 claws of a window are i.i.d., independent of the chaining value and of the number of claws, and a claw's trial-key count is a function of its (a0, a1) only (W8..W11, hence F8, do not depend on the chaining value); the W17 claw constants (w, c) are uniform and independent of (a0, u), as H5 uses. This is a new premise of ae2d3c1c, kept: 9,044.1 is the joint one-sided 99% lower bound of Section 7, from the keys per F9 claw measured on 0b62ed88's unscreened claws (one-way ANOVA of the 2,000 claws' key counts over their 16 windows: F = 0.564 on 15 and 1,984 df) and the distinct F9 claws per window measured on the 60 screened windows, with C_W as the declared model mean; the screen conditions the chaining value on S <= 5, so the unscreened law does not transfer by itself; the premise declares it. Support (participant-run, paired, same seeds on both builds; 16 seed pairs, 2^24 walk evaluations, harness winmeasure_rival.py; N = F8-passing listed entries and K = distinct keys among them over the four diagnostic groups 0, 50, 100, 150 of k4f, per distinct claw C): unscreened N/C 106.91, K/C 98.56; screened N/C 111.16, K/C 102.24; paired N/C change +0.0552 bit (s.e. 0.0459). Distinct F9 claws per window: 907.17 (s.d. 25.68) in the 60 screened 2^26 windows against 898.62 in the 48 unscreened ones. This probe supports a nonnegative transfer of the yield; it is not a 2^26 panel of the key count, and the transfer of the unscreened keys-per-F9-claw count to the screened law is the declared premise.
- **H1-ops.** The constants of Sections 3 and 5; the pass is a constant of the program; the screen charges 4 + 183 per draw and 3 per discarded draw.
- **H2-transfer (MODEL, declared, favorable; new in this entry; screened scope).** p_tail >= 2^-74.3238 for the designated (lowest-a3) F8 mate of a trial key drawn uniformly over all trial (window, claw, key) triples of the attack, windows drawn under the screened chaining-value law of Section 3.6 and weighted by their trial count, in a claw passing F9 with W17 hit: the linear mean of the 14 organizer runs r39-tail-01..14 on the advice draws, carried to the fibre 0x3cc9eebe. Evidence: the paired transfer arm (-0.014 bit, s.e. 0.023); arm K (mean 2^-74.3734, s.e. 0.0364; weighted by window size, one-sided 99.9% bound 2^-74.5058) and arm R 3cc9eebe (mean 2^-74.3781), participant-run, both below the priced value, on claws of unscreened windows; the earlier new-fibre measurements and acceptance are of the unscreened law, and the premise extends the value to keys of screened windows. Model, stated plainly: the SMC carrier of the arm sees a window only through its claws' (a0, a1); the words W0..W7 of the chaining value are free in it, as in every earlier tail arm.
- **H3-advice-construction.** As in w13; for every listed entry of the new fibre both messages follow the advice trail through step 15 (enum15 on all entries; the organizer run on one entry of every group).
- **H5-group-independence (screened-window scope).** For the windows of the screened law: windows independent (fresh first blocks, each drawn and screened independently); trials are distinct keys with an entry in F8, at least 9041.6 per distinct claw (H1-screen); (iv) at most 944 distinct F9 claws are admitted per window (program cap, this entry's change; a26bcf74: 1,024); (v) the i.i.d./independence of the claws' (a0, a1) and the trial-key count per claw are declared for the FIRST 944 admitted distinct F9 claws of a window in arrival order (MODEL; the organizer windows never reach the cap); each listed key's W17 event has probability 2^-32 in each claw; events of different claws are independent. Within a claw, two keys hit together iff G(a2, kappa, w) = s0(a2 + w) - (a2 + w) + kappa coincide. Let N_k(w) be the number of other listed keys with G equal to key k's at the claw's w, and pi_k = E_w[N_k(w)]. Measured over all 3,462,264 listed keys on two independent sets of 16,384 random w: mean pi 1.07e-3, largest per-key estimate 4.6e-3; per-(key, w) counts on the second set: N = 1 in 60,723,478 cases, N = 2 in 37,173, N = 3 in 40, N >= 4 in none of 5.67e10. At the w of 2,000 real F9 claws of 0b62ed88's unscreened program: mean pi 1.0825e-3, largest per-(key, w) N = 3 (w15/critic_final/cohit_real.c, cohit_real_2000.txt; w and u at all 43,134 real claws in wreal.py, wreal.txt). The claw's w contains -cv5 additively, so it is uniform and independent of (a0, u) under H1-screen. Hits whose equal-G cluster in the claw has more than 4 keys are left out of the second-order sum; for every kept key N_k <= 3, and family-wise over all keys (alpha = 0.001) E[min(N_k, 3)] <= 1.36e-2. Left-out hits cost at most P(N_k >= 4) <= ln(3,462,264 / 0.001) / 16,384 = 1.341e-3 per key in the first-order term (no N >= 4 for any key in 16,384 w; family-wise over all keys at alpha = 0.001). Both bounds hold for every key, so the within-claw term holds whatever the relation between a key's partner rate and its tail. The claw's W17 constants (w, c) are independent of the designated-mate tail events, as for the hit events themselves. 37 real 2^-32 key hits were observed against 38.58 expected (Section 7).
- **H6-cap-completion.** Section 7: the screened whole-window bound, a model-based 99.75% bound on the mean (and on the s.d.) of the screened window work under the stated window-distribution model.
- **H-implicit-distinct-key-dispersion.** Tested in the organizer run at a scaled event over all keys of four groups in every F9 claw (Section 11).
- **Limits of the evidence.** The cap sample is 60 screened windows of the shipped attack path on public seeds; the keys per F9 claw are our 2,000 claws of 0b62ed88's unscreened windows, carried to the screened law by H1-screen, and the F9 claws per window are the 60 screened windows: participant-run. The organizer run counts F8-passing keys and their scaled dispersion on four fixed groups of the 200 (22 claws); it is a spot test at probability 2^-7 and does not establish independence of the 2^-32 events over all groups and all windows, which remains the premise H5. The tail replica the organizer runs samples the advice distribution; the transfer to the new fibre rests on the participant-run 28-run arms (paired -0.014, s.e. 0.023; direct 99.9% bound 2^-74.4804 on the new fibre). The memory claim is a peak over phases. No full collision has been executed; every experiment is a component test.

## 11. Experiments (organizer sandbox; every organizer-run value is hard-asserted by the program)
- `r39-transplant-claw`, trial 0: the advice collides under 39 steps; the advice-construction checks of Section 9; and for the sample entry of each of the 200 groups at the advice point: the rule holds, W9 = advice W9 + 0x05cefde0, W16 one value, both messages follow the advice trail through step 16 and message 1 the advice states from A[8], E[12] (200 of 200). Every further trial: a random chaining value and claw-free (a0, u) with a listed entry of the fibre: transplant states, W1 = u and W16 - g = F(u) - F(a0).
- `r39k4-window-small`, trials 0-3: windows of 2^21 evaluations, check mode, k4 on for every F9 claw (7, 11, 4, 1 claws). Every claw asserts W9 = C9 + HD - a1 = W9 of a listed entry and W16 = g. The pass runs over all 62,400 lanes. Asserted tuples (claws, F9, 0, pass lanes, survivors, key hits, k4 ops, total ops): (233,7,0,436800,2,0,1019221,11504962), (222,11,0,624000,5,0,1454268,13875066), (256,4,0,249600,2,0,584630,13031225), (232,1,0,62400,0,0,144113,11245985). Each k4 ops value is (evaluated F9 claws, pass lanes / 62,400) x (143,633 + 480), plus 12 per repeated F9 claw (the dedupe lookup), plus 10,430 for its 2 real survivors; 13,126 for its 5 real survivors; 8,178 for its 2 real survivors. Each trial emits k4_setup = 1,107,473,556.
  - The four asserted windows run with the screen off (`screen=0`; the k4 path is the same code with the screen on or off), so their tuples are 0b62ed88's.
  - Pass-off control: trials 0 and 1 are re-run with k4 off; claws and F9 equal, ops_off = ops - k4_ops.
  - Screened window (trial 0, same seed, screen on as on the attack path): asserted that the window is not skipped, the kept chaining value has S <= 5, every draw is charged 187 operations (kept) or 190 (discarded), and the discarded-draw count equals the number of draws with S > 5. On the organizer seed of trial 0: 12 draws, 11 discarded, kept S = 1, (claws, F9, total ops) = (258, 1, 10,371,107). No new output key.
  - Planted check on the first F9 claw of each window, for each of the 200 groups: the key is found and its counted cost is asserted.
  - Key dispersion over all entries of every 50th group (4 groups), all F9 claws: per claw D = keys with an entry in F8, K = those whose W17 x 2654435761 mod 2^32 has its top 7 bits zero (probability 2^-7). Asserted per trial (sum D, sum K, Pearson, claws): (59,256, 437, 6.5188, 7); (67,492, 518, 7.9839, 10); (17,882, 142, 0.7772, 4); (1,872, 7, 4.0067, 1). Pooled 146,502 key events, 1,104 hits against 1144.5 expected (z = -1.20), Pearson 19.29 on 22 claws. Acceptance region, asserted on the sums: sum D >= 96,821, |sum K - sum D/128| within 2.576 s.d., Pearson < 40.29 (99% quantile, 22 dof).
- `r39-tail-01..14`: the replica with QDECL = -74.54, unchanged.
- Local seed sets, run by this entry with the same program and code path: 11 sets of 4 windows with seeds fixed before any run (sha256 of `w15-dispersion|setNN|i`), 138 claws, 6,693 hits against 6675.6 expected (z = +0.21), Pearson 126.68 on 138 degrees of freedom; the largest set value is z = +1.43. On the organizer seeds the largest per-claw |z| is 2.00.
- Run by this entry (tools, not in the package): 48 full windows (Appendix A); 2,000 claws (Section 7); the exhaustive and end-to-end checks of Section 2; the memory audit of Section 6; the walk-kernel generator on 300 chaining values (Section 6). Run for this derivative's screened program (MEASURED, participant-run): the 60 screened windows of Appendix B; the paired 2^24 yield probe of H1-screen. Linux (WSL) wall time of each experiment of the shipped program in the organizer form: r39-transplant-claw 1.50 s, r39k4-window-small 13.05 s, r39-tail runs at most 19.62 s.
